plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Add to QQQI to increase income exposure.
Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration.
Hold remaining positions with tight stops.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, holding a larger cash buffer for stability and lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration.
Buy AAPL as a new, high-scoring addition.
Trim QQQ and CRWD to reduce concentration.
Maintain a balanced mix of broad index and quality tech.
balanced.read: This plan aims for risk-first growth with a target of around 2.5% per month. It balances reducing leverage and concentration with adding a strong new name, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL.
Add AAPL as a new, high-conviction name.
Increase position in CRWD, a strong performer.
Trim SMH to reduce exposure to underperforming semiconductors.
Concentrate heavily in top-scoring tech and leveraged plays.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring tech names. Expect higher potential upside but also substantially larger drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses due to leverage and ETF decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Significantly increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to free up capital.
Sell high-beta single names like CRWD and SMH.
Focus on steady monthly distributions and capital preservation.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month, prioritizing steady distributions over growth. It shifts heavily into income-generating ETFs like QQQI and cuts all high-beta and leveraged positions. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
